newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity regulator cuts fossil fuel levy.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity regulator cuts fossil fuel levy.

text.p: Britain's Office of Electricity Regulation (Offer) said on Friday it would cut a levy it imposes on licensed electricity suppliers, known as the fossil fuel levy, to 2.2 percent of customer billings, from 3.7 percent.

The change will take place from April 1, 1997, Offer said in a statement. It added that, following the flotation earlier this year of nuclear generator British Energy Plc, a levy in respect of nuclear commitments would cease from April 1, 1998.
The levy is a form of cross-subsidy intended to cover the electricity industry's commitments to contract renewable energy generating capacity.
